children: reported a 31% rise in annual profit on Monday, driven by management of margins, capital and costs, as well as business growth.

ANZ, Australia's fourth-largest lender by market capitalisation, posted cash profit of A$7.59 billion ($5.21 billion) for the year ended September 30, in line with a Visible Alpha consensus of A$7.55 billion and above last year's A$5.79 billion.
Operating expenses declined 14% in fiscal 2026 due to lower restructuring expenses and the absence of the Australian Securities and Investments Commission settlement amount
The Australia Retail division's annual cash profit climbed to A$1.71 billion from A$771 million last year, lifted by higher home loan volumes
Net loans and advances for the Australia Retail division stood at A$280 billion as at September end, up from A$269 billion last year
Net interest margin, a key measure of profitability, slid marginally to 1.53%, hurt by competition across most divisions and the timing of Reserve Bank of Australia rate changes
The Reserve Bank of Australia lifted interest rates by 25 basis points to 4.85% last week, the highest since December 2008, in a 6-3 vote
ANZ's common equity tier 1 ratio, a measure of spare cash, slipped to 12.0% as of the financial year-end
It declared a final dividend of 83 Australian cents per share, matching last year's payout
